properties.evidence: It opposes the HYPOTHESIS that record carried, not its measurement. The 448 MB reading stands as taken. What is refuted is the explanation offered with it — six ALL_CFS column families at Options::default() giving ~384 MB of memtable — which the baseline record deliberately filed as arithmetic from source rather than as a cause. A fresh server on an identical 4,403-node store with those exact defaults measures 62 MB. The refutation is therefore of the RocksDB clause and of the work it implied (tune write buffers, share a block cache, cap open files), which addresses 43 MB rather than 400 MB. Note the limit: this was measured on reflow2's own 14.7 MB export, and it does NOT account for 448 MB on flo2's 2.9 MB design, which stays unexplained.
